Evolve a population

Source: R/evolve.R
evolve.Rd

Runs a population through a list of selection regimes. Starting from a model creates a new population of n individuals; starting from a population continues it (same individuals, generation count, optimum and recorded statistics).

Usage

evolve(x, regimes, ...)

# S3 method for class 'evomod_model'
evolve(x, regimes, n, record_every = 1, seed = NULL, initial = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'evomod_population'
evolve(x, regimes, record_every = x$record_every, seed = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

an evomod_model (new population) or an evomod_population (continue it).

regimes

a regime or a list of regimes, see regimes.

...

further arguments for the methods.

n

population size.

record_every

record population statistics every this many generations (and at the start).

seed

optional seed passed to set.seed() before the run.

initial

optional starting genomes, an array rows x alleles x n (see genomes()); by default they are drawn as described in evomod_model().

Value

An evomod_population; see trait_means(), g_matrices() and variances() for the recorded statistics.

Details

Each generation: the optimum moves (directional regimes), fitness is computed from the current phenotypes, every individual mutates, n pairs of parents are drawn with probability proportional to fitness (with replacement), and each offspring gets one random allele per locus from each parent (free recombination). Random numbers come from R's generator, so set.seed() (or seed) makes runs reproducible.

Examples

model <- evomod_model(additive(loci = 20, traits = 2),
                      mutation(rate = 0.01, cov = 0.1), env_sd = 1, init_sd = 0.1)
pop <- evolve(model, n = 100, regimes = list(stabilizing(50, omega = 10)),
              record_every = 10, seed = 1)
pop <- evolve(pop, directional(50, delta_theta = c(0.02, 0), omega = 10))
trait_means(pop)
